subject: social_science
chapter_title: Early Humans and Beginning of Civilisation

concepts.title: Life of Early Humans: Hunting-Gathering
concepts.definition: Before civilisation, humans lived as hunting-gathering bands, moving with seasons and animals, using stone tools and fire, and leaving their story in rock paintings and tool sites that archaeologists excavate.
concepts.key_idea: Move, hunt, gather, adapt: early life followed the rhythm of nature.
concepts.textbook_ref: iest104.txt opening sections (how humans lived before civilisation)
question_patterns: how did humans live before the beginning of civilisation
what did early humans eat and how did they get it
why did early humans keep moving from place to place
what role did fire and stone tools play in their life
what do rock paintings tell us about early humans
how do archaeologists learn about hunter-gatherers

solution_steps.explain: Hunting animals and gathering food sustained small mobile bands.
Stone tools and fire changed what humans could eat and where they could live.
Tools, bones and paintings are the evidence of this age.

concepts.title: The Agricultural Revolution
concepts.definition: Learning to grow crops and tame animals transformed human life: farming fixed people to fields, surplus food supported larger settlements, and villages grew where hunting bands had wandered - the first step towards civilisation.
concepts.key_idea: Seeds changed history: agriculture rooted people and produced surplus.
concepts.textbook_ref: iest104.txt sections on the beginning of farming
question_patterns: how did farming begin - describe the transition
why is the beginning of agriculture called a revolution
what changes did farming bring to human life
name the early crops and domesticated animals
how did surplus food change society
compare the life of hunter-gatherers and early farmers

solution_steps.explain: Observing growth cycles led to deliberate sowing.
Fields tied families to one place; huts became villages.
Extra grain freed some people for crafts and leadership.

concepts.title: The Beginning of Civilisation
concepts.definition: Civilisation flowered where surplus, cities and organisation met: river valleys supported writing, monumental building, craft specialisation, trade and organised states - marking a decisive new stage in the human story.
concepts.key_idea: Surplus built cities, cities demanded writing and states: civilisation's toolkit.
concepts.textbook_ref: iest104.txt sections on the beginning of civilisation
question_patterns: what are the markers of a civilisation
why did civilisations grow in river valleys
what is the role of writing in a civilisation
how did cities differ from villages in early civilisations
name the features common to early civilisations
explain the link between surplus and specialisation

solution_steps.explain: Cities, writing, crafts, trade and organised rule mark civilisations.
Fertile silt and water made surplus reliable.
Managers, scribes and rulers coordinated the complex society.

questions: Describe the life of hunting-gathering communities.
